verdict.rationale: Glama's hosted API reference has a per-endpoint "Try it" panel that sends real requests from the browser. Each endpoint also has cURL/JavaScript/Python/PHP samples and full schemas, all backed by a published OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec that the API catalog makes discoverable. The 404s on generic OpenAPI paths do not contradict this, because the spec lives at /api/mcp/openapi.json. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the Try-it runner, and a sandbox or test-key mode (the runner hits the production API with a real bearer key).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: The vendor-hosted API reference carries a per-endpoint "Try it" panel ("Requests are sent directly from this browser. Credentials are never stored.") alongside cURL/JavaScript/Python/PHP samples and full schemas.
The RFC 9727 API catalog (application/linkset+json) links the machine spec (service-desc) and the hosted reference (service-doc)
Glama publishes an OpenAPI 3.0.3 document for its MCP directory API
